items.label: SK Telecom press release: SK Telecom Launches AI Data Center Infrastructure Company (08-27-2026)
items.signal_prefix: SK Telecom will split its wholly owned subsidiary

set.signal: SK Telecom will split its wholly owned subsidiary SK Broadband into a surviving company and a new company, SK Horizon, which takes over SK Broadband's data center and submarine cable businesses. SK Horizon will expand its infrastructure to a total capacity of 318 MW, covering eight data centers already in operation (Seocho, Ilsan (2 locations), Bundang, Gasan, Centum, Yangju and Pangyo) and new AIDCs under construction including Ulsan and Guro, and will pursue phased expansion of submarine cable infrastructure. SKT will oversee the group's AIDC strategy and collaborate with global big tech companies; SK Hyper (established in July) will develop new AIDC projects, with 5 GW of capacity targeted for phased opening in 2029 and expansion toward a total of 15 GW in 2035. The spin-off and new company are targeted for the first quarter of next year, subject to an extraordinary shareholders' meeting and government approvals.

items.reason: Remove the ownership outcome of the KKR / IMM KRW 3.08tn equity deal (SKT 51% largest shareholder); financing terms themselves were already excluded.
items.evidence: SKT will retain management control as the largest shareholder with a 51% stake.
